digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and digest history event store
propositions: Deleting committed enrichment/digest UUID events triggers git rename-detection conflicts on merge, making deletion-based retention unsafe even though it does not reclaim repository space

The queue reduce is O(history) file opens because _events_of opens and parses every matching file; the read bound can be fixed to ≤3+k file opens per ticket by reading newest-first UUID-named suffix instead

No retention scheme that physically deletes or renames committed UUID events is safe under invariant I1 without amending the invariant deliberately; rename-safe retention requires deterministic source-derived paths with identical content

The measured cost of enrichment/digest accumulation is <2% of working tree checkout; physical prune reclaims zero repository space while adding merge conflicts and commits, making read-bound design strictly superior
The designed suffix-lazy reader changes only reader behavior and preserves every committed event byte-for-byte, guaranteeing unchanged cross-clone merge behavior and reconvergence
